findings.cross_file_justification: The gate in loader.py (diff-touched) decides whether complete() in agy_headless_adapter.py (diff-touched) places the redacted review prompt on a world-readable argv. The adapter's own comments state the caller's cwd is the reviewed tree and treat that tree as untrusted (private workspace, refusal of any GEMINI.md). The gate reads its answer from that same tree.
findings.description: agy_opt_in_enabled() resolves the project root by walking up from the current working directory and reads hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in from the .loa.config.yaml found there (plus .claude/defaults system defaults merged under it). In the review flows this code serves (Bridgebuilder, flatline, adversarial-review), the cwd is the checked-out tree under review, as the agy adapter's own comments state. A pull request can therefore add or edit .loa.config.yaml with `hounfour:\n  headless:\n    agy_opt_in: true` and re-enable the argv-prompt route without any operator action. The docstring frames the gate as closing ambient influence ("no environment override"), but the config layer it trusts is equally ambient in a CI review of an untrusted branch. The test test_the_project_root_defaults_to_the_cwd_walk pins this behavior as intended.
findings.failure_mode: An untrusted branch flips the privacy-sensitive agy route on. The reviewed diff (which may contain secrets scrubbed only by redaction) is then passed on the agy CLI's argv and is readable by every local account via /proc/<pid>/cmdline and ps for the life of the hop. The one-time WARN fires, but no operator consented. This undermines the FR-1 guarantee that the exposure is "only ever exposed by an operator's deliberate choice".
findings.suggested_fix: Read the opt-in from an operator-owned location that a reviewed branch cannot write: e.g. a user/host config (~/.config/loa or an explicit path from the orchestrator), or require the orchestrator script to pass the decision explicitly after reading it from a trusted checkout (the base branch, not the PR head). Alternatively, when the cwd-walked project root differs from the installed Loa root or the git base ref, treat agy_opt_in as false and log why. Add a test that a config found only in the reviewed tree does not enable the route.

findings.description: build_headless_argv appends `--effort <value>` for any truthy string without checking it against the allowed levels. It is now a shared builder used by both the adapter (via _resolve_effort, which also reads operator-supplied extra.effort) and the ceiling probe. The cheval CLI chokepoint (resolve_effort) validates its own inputs, but the builder trusts every caller, so a future caller or a malformed catalog value reaches the child process argv unchecked.
findings.failure_mode: A non-level string lands on the claude CLI argv. Today's callers are operator-controlled, so this is not exploitable by review content, but a value beginning with `-` would be parsed by the CLI as a flag and change the headless invocation shape the builder is meant to pin.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate `effort` inside build_headless_argv against the same tuple cheval.py uses (_EFFORT_LEVELS, or a shared constant in loa_cheval.types) and raise ConfigError on anything else. Also assert `not cli_model.startswith('-')` since the model label is likewise operator config placed directly on argv.
